concerns_addressed: PaymentService::record now delegates the transaction body to cohesive helpers without changing the transaction boundary, outlet-then-order lock ordering, post-lock idempotency lookup, validation, persistence, receipt generation, or order mutation behavior.

The concurrent public HTTP race remains covered by two independent PHP workers and the filesystem barrier. PaymentTest passes with one payment row, identical replayed payment IDs, 201/200 success responses, and exactly one order balance mutation.
Idempotency replay validates authorization, order identity, and amount; unique-key fallback reloads the committed winner rather than returning a 500.

Payment recording remains transaction-wrapped, so receipt-generation failure rolls back payment, receipt state, order balance/status, and status history. Partial payments, overpayment rejection, delivered-status enforcement, and non-negative outstanding balances remain intact.

Credit enforcement still occurs at order submission under the outlet lock, includes New/Confirmed/Delivered/Partially Paid outstanding orders, blocks zero and cumulative over-limit submissions before order or stock mutation, and exposes the expected outstanding calculation.
PaymentTest passes all 7 tests and 75 assertions; the complete API suite passes all 43 tests and 262 assertions.

strengths: PaymentService::record is now a short retry/orchestration method; recordInTransaction, locking, replay, validation, balance calculation, record creation, and order mutation are separated into cohesive private helpers, all clearing the prior approximately 95-line heuristic.
The refactor preserves consistent outlet-before-order locking with order creation and keeps all financial mutations and status-history writes inside one transaction.
Money calculations remain normalized to integer cents, with bounded response balances and atomic partial/full payment status updates.
Authorization and outlet scoping are preserved for payment recording, payment reads, and credit-limit reads/configuration.
The critical path has real HTTP concurrency regression coverage and the full API regression suite is green.
